children.value: The softening model simulates pellet softening processes used for water hardness removal. It combines chemical dosing with precipitation reactions and includes bypass flow control and acid neutralization for pH adjustment.
The softening model inherits from both the base
class, enabling it to handle mass balance calculations and chemical precipitation processes.
The model calculates flow distribution between reactor and bypass:

children.value: The softening process follows these sequential steps:
- Combination of softened and bypass flows
Acid is added to the softened water before mixing:

children.html: Solutionneutralized=Solutionsoftened+Aciddose\text{Solution}_{neutralized} = \text{Solution}_{softened} + \text{Acid}_{dose}Solutionneutralized​=Solutionsoftened​+Aciddose​

children.value: Acid is added to the bypass flow:

children.html: Solutionneutralized=Solutionbypass+Aciddose\text{Solution}_{neutralized} = \text{Solution}_{bypass} + \text{Acid}_{dose}Solutionneutralized​=Solutionbypass​+Aciddose​

children.value: Acid is added to the mixed flow:

children.html: Solutionneutralized=Solutionmixed+Aciddose\text{Solution}_{neutralized} = \text{Solution}_{mixed} + \text{Acid}_{dose}Solutionneutralized​=Solutionmixed​+Aciddose​

children.value: The final effluent is a mixture of softened and bypass flows:

children.html: Solutionmixed=Solutionsoftened×(1−fbypass)+Solutionbypass×fbypass\text{Solution}_{mixed} = \text{Solution}_{softened} \times (1 - f_{bypass}) + \text{Solution}_{bypass} \times f_{bypass}Solutionmixed​=Solutionsoftened​×(1−fbypass​)+Solutionbypass​×fbypass​
